court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: State Rep by, Sub Inspector of Police, Podhanur Police Station, Coimbatore and Others
case_number: Crl.O.P. No. 6002 of 2026 and Crl.M.P. No. 4412 of 2026
advocates: For R 1 : Mr. Leonard Arul Joseph Selvam, Additional Public Prosecutor
For R 2 : Mr. S. Dharma Dhurai
prayer: Prayer: Criminal Original Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to call for the records in Crime No. 98/2025 dated 12-3-2025 on the file of the 1st respondent Police and quash the same.
judgment_text:
ORDER

1. The petitioner/accused in Crime No. 98 of 2025 for offence under Sections 296(b) and 115 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhitam, 2023 on the file of the respondent Police has filed this Criminal Original Petition.

2. Case of the prosecution is that the 2nd respondent was working as a contract Sanitary Supervisor in Ward No. 85, South Zone, Coimbatore Corporation. On 12-3-2025, the petitioner, a permanent Sanitary Worker working in Ward No. 34, Central Zone along with contract workers Suguna and Kamala entered the office without any permission and abused the 2nd respondent in filthy language and also grabbed his shirt in front of employees. On the complaint of the 2nd respondent, the 1st respondent Police registered an FIR in Crime No. 98 of 2025 for offence under Sections 296(b) and 115 of BNS, 2023 against the petitioner.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner did not involve in any activities as alleged by the 2nd respondent and he did not use filthy language or physical violence against the 2nd respondent. He further submits that on considering the well-being and future, the 2nd respondent is not willing to proceed further with the complaint registered against the petitioner. Both the petitioner and the 2nd respondent arrived at a compromise and resolved the issue. Hence, he prays for quashing.

4. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the 1st respondent Police submitted that on 12-3-2025, the petitioner, a permanent Sanitary Worker working in Ward No. 34, Central Zone along with contract workers Suguna and Kamala, entered the 2nd respondent's office without any permission and abused the 2nd respondent in filthy language and also grabbed his shirt in front of employees. On the complaint of the 2nd respondent, the respondent Police registered an FIR in Crime No. 98 of 2025 for offence under Sections 296(b) and 115 of BNS, 2023 against the petitioner. Now the investigation is going-on. In the meantime, both the petitioner and the 2nd respondent arrived at a compromise and settled the issues.

5. Considering the submissions and on perusal of mateirals, it is seen that the case is still at the stage of investigation. By passage of time, the parties have decided to bury their hatchet and compromise the dispute amicably among themselves.

6. Today the petitioner and the 2nd respondent appeared before this Court and their identity is confirmed by Mr Madasamy, Sub Inspector of Police attached to the 1st respondent Police Station. This Court also enquired both the parties and was satisfied that the parties have come to an amicable settlement between themselves. The petitioner and the 2nd respondent have filed separate affidavit before this Court and also filed the Joint Compromise memo.

7. Under such circumstances, no useful purpose will be served in keeping the first information report pending, even though, the offences involved are not compoundable in nature. In the light of the guidelines given by the Supreme Court reported in (2017) 9 SCC 641 : (2018) 1 SCC (Cri) 1-(Parbathbhai Aahir @ Parbathbhai v. State of Gujrath ), and after exercising due caution as advised by the Hon'ble Suprme Court in The State of Madhya Pradesh v. Dhruv Gurjar, (2019) 2 Mad LJ (Cri) 10), this Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC quashes the first information report on the file of the 1st respondent Police.

8. This Criminal Original Petition stands allowed and as a sequel, the investigation in Crime No. 98 of 2025, on the file of the 1st respondent police, is quashed against the petitioner. Consequently, connected Criminal Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
